newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed curtails Idaho remediation project.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed curtails Idaho remediation project.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp is curtailing remediation activities at a U.S. Department of Energy laboratory in Idaho where it has demonstrated a waste retrieval and treatment system.

Under a $179 million contract, the company was to remediate a site known as Pit 9, originally believed to contain 150,000 cubic feet of plutonium-contaminated waste buried between 1967 and 1969, Lockheed said in a statement on Friday.
"The job we're being asked to do today is not the job we contracted for in 1994," James Tegnelia, president of Lockheed Martin Advanced Environmental Systems, said in a statement.

Lockheed Martin said it was scaling back the project until it could obtain adequate technical guidance from the Energy Department about the contents of pit, a schedule for removing the waste, the estimated cost and safety issues.

The company said it notified 115 Lockheed Martin employees and subcontractors involved in the project about the situation at the site, located at the Idaho National Engineering and Environment Laboratory in Pocatello.
A permanent shutdown may be necessary if it cannot resolve the outstanding issues, it said.
Lockheed Martin said the technology for the project has been proven in laboratory testing but never used to treat the types of materials now believed to be present at the site.
